title: Chew Away Your Worries? Teens Invent Anxiety-Fighting Gum!
summary: Have you ever chewed gum to calm down before a big test? Two teens from Georgia took that idea and ran with it — all the way to a giant science fair! Zackary Nizker and Sara Hoti, both 16, invented a chewing gum that could help fight anxiety. Anxiety is that worried, nervous feeling that just won't go away. About one in three teens deal with it, Zackary says. His grandma also struggles with severe nervousness, and the medicine she took had scary side effects. So the pair turned to a plant that grows wild in their hometown: passionflower. This plant has natural chemicals called flavonoids (say: FLAY-vuh-noyds) that can calm the brain. They work by boosting a brain signal called GABA, which slows down over-excited brain cells. The teens mixed passionflower extract into homemade bubble gum. But they couldn't just hand it out to friends — that's not safe. Instead, they did clever lab tests. First, they checked if every piece of gum had the same amount of extract. Under a microscope, they saw the particles were spread evenly — a perfect score! Next, they tested if the flavonoids would survive chewing. They soaked gum pieces in alcohol to mimic saliva, but the flavonoids stayed locked inside. That's actually good: it means the gum might release them slowly as you chew. Their project earned them a spot at the 2026 Regeneron International Science & Engineering Fair (ISEF), where over 1,700 kids from 65 countries competed. Zackary and Sara won fourth place in their category and a $600 prize. Next, they hope to test the gum on real people to see if it truly eases anxiety. Who knows? Someday, calming nerves might be as easy as popping a piece of gum!
why_it_matters: Feeling anxious is common for many kids, and a simple invention like gum could someday help them calm down in a safe, natural way.

background_read: Many kids feel nervous sometimes, and some plants like chamomile or lavender have been used for centuries to help people relax.
The Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (also called ISEF) is the world’s largest pre-college science competition, where students from many countries show off their projects.
Passionflower has been used in traditional medicine for anxiety and sleep problems, but scientists are still studying how well it works.
Article_Structure: WHO: Zackary Nizker and Sara Hoti, two 16-year-olds from Georgia.
WHAT: They invented a chewing gum with passionflower extract to help fight anxiety.
WHERE: At the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF).
WHY: Because one in three teens deal with anxiety, and Zackary’s grandma had bad side effects from anxiety medicine.

perspectives.description: This gum could provide a natural, side-effect-free way to manage anxiety, helping millions of teens and adults.
The gum has only been tested in lab experiments so far; it might not work on real people, or it could have unknown effects.
The invention shows how young scientists can explore plants for health solutions, but more research is needed before it becomes a real product.
